synopsis: This 1963 National Bureau of Standards film documents the development of Peru’s Jicamarca Observatory, from the search for a site near the magnetic equator through construction of its 22-acre antenna and powerful radar system. It explains how incoherent-scatter radar measures electrons in the upper atmosphere and highlights cooperation between U.S. researchers, Peru’s Instituto Geofísico del Perú, and local workers and technicians.
